requirement:
HC represents a FIXME acknowledgment as a graph node and exposes its tracking
issue relationships as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes. A named FIXME also
connects the acknowledgment to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges;
an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
Each issue named by the acknowledgment is available through its tracking edges.
rationale: Add tests, each marked {test}`requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph`. The first test should read a named FIXME acknowledgment node. It should assert that the node has tracking edges to each GitHub issue it names, and that it has an edge to the requirement node whose gap it acknowledges. The second test should read an unnamed FIXME acknowledgment. It should assert that the node connects directly to its tracking issues and has no requirement edge. Include a case where the FIXME names multiple issues, and assert that every issue is reachable through its tracking edges. Assert the edge labels too, not only the targets. — I found no {test} reference, :test: anchor, or Tests edge for `requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph`. A text search of the project, and of `tests/` for FIXME or acknowledgment, found only tests for other requirements. Those are the authoring and CLI FIXME-evidence tests in `tests/authoring_batch.rs`. They check determinations and issue states, not the graph representation. Nothing tests any obligation of the subject. The obligations are: a FIXME is a graph node, it exposes tracking edges to GitHub issue nodes, a named FIXME connects to its requirement, an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its issues, and every named issue is available through a tracking edge. The `{fixme}` on `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` names nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26. The supplied acknowledgment records that issue as closed, so it no longer acknowledges the gap. The gap is therefore unacknowledged.
